summary: Finance: guidance needed on interpreting cached-token cost fields in Usage Insights exports (CSV/JSON)
description:
Requestor: Finance (Rishi)

Context
Finance is preparing internal guidance for how to use the new Usage Insights export reports (CSV + JSON) for chargeback and month-end cost review.

Question / ask
In exported reports we have fields related to caching (e.g., cached tokens). Finance needs an authoritative explanation of:
- What “cached tokens” represent in the export (prefix/KV cache / response cache) and whether they are always a subset of input tokens.
- Whether cached tokens are billed differently than non-cached tokens.
- How to reconcile:
  1) total_cost
  2) input/output token counts
  3) cached token counts
  4) unit cost fields
- How to explain scenarios where cached-token counts are present but the effective cost reduction is not obvious at the route rollup level.

Impact
- Blocking Finance from publishing internal documentation for interpreting exports.
- Risk of incorrect chargeback allocations and avoidable escalations to Support.

Where this shows up
Usage Insights -> Export report (route/model breakdown) -> CSV/JSON

Proposed owner routing
Telemetry/Cost attribution + PM to confirm canonical definitions and billing behavior.

Acceptance criteria
- Written definitions for cached token fields and how they roll up into total_cost.
- 2–3 examples that Finance can paste into their internal guidance.
- Any known limitations or caveats (late data, rounding, aggregation windows).

References
- Project: In-console usage insights (cost drivers by route)
- Prior customer confusion about “invoice vs console” and “missing route tags” suggests we should be explicit about what’s included/excluded.
comments:
2026-02-20 10:14 PT — Rishi Malhotra (Reporter)
We’re drafting a one-pager for Finance/RevOps on how to interpret the new export fields. The cached token columns are tripping people up. Specifically: do cached tokens reduce billed tokens, or are they billed at a different rate, or are they informational only? We need a crisp definition + how it ties to total_cost so we don’t publish something incorrect.

2026-02-20 13:02 PT — Dev Patel (Support readiness)
Looping in because we’ve already seen similar confusion in customer tickets (invoice vs console). Even if Finance-only today, this should likely become a short FAQ in docs. Assigning to PM/Telemetry for authoritative wording.

2026-02-21 09:36 PT — Nadia Rahman (Telemetry)
Cached tokens in the exports are intended to represent tokens served without full incremental compute due to caching (primarily prefix/KV cache reuse). They should be treated as a subset of input-side work; in some flows we can attribute “cached input tokens” distinctly. The pricing model can differ by deployment / contract, so we should align on language that doesn’t over-promise. Paula—can you confirm the product-facing phrasing we want?

2026-02-21 11:18 PT — Paula Mendes (Assignee)
Proposed canonical wording (please sanity check):
1) Token counts: input_tokens + output_tokens represent total tokens processed/returned for the request. cached_input_tokens represents the portion of input tokens whose compute was avoided due to cache reuse.
2) Cost fields: total_cost is the amount attributed by metering for the time window/filters. If cached tokens are eligible for discounted compute attribution, that effect is already reflected in total_cost (i.e., you don’t need to manually subtract cached tokens).
3) Unit costs: unit_cost fields are derived from total_cost / (billable token basis) and can differ by plan.
Caveats: aggregation rounding, late-arriving metering, and mixed model/fallback can make savings not appear as a simple per-token discount in route rollups.
Nadia/Logan: confirm whether we should say “billable tokens” anywhere vs keep it generic as “attributed cost”.

2026-02-22 15:47 PT — Logan Wright (Telemetry/Analytics EM)
+1 to keeping this as “attributed cost” for now. Internally, the pipeline calculates total_cost using the metering events and the customer’s pricing configuration; cached token fields are supplemental diagnostics to explain why two routes with similar total tokens might have different cost.
Suggested example to include:
- Route A and Route B both have 10M input tokens, but Route A has 6M cached_input_tokens due to repeated system prompts; Route A’s total_cost is lower because cached tokens reduced GPU-time proxy (or token pricing) depending on the contract.
Also note: cached_input_tokens may be 0 if cache visibility is not available for a given request path/model runtime even if caching occurs; we should call that out as a limitation.

2026-02-23 10:08 PT — Rishi Malhotra (Reporter)
This is helpful. For Finance docs we can avoid plan-specific claims and stick to “already reflected in total_cost.” Can we also add one sentence on reconciliation: total_cost in exports should match (or be within small deltas of) the same filtered view in console, but may differ from invoices due to invoicing cutoffs/credits/other charges?

2026-02-24 09:22 PT — Paula Mendes (Assignee)
Confirmed. Adding a reconciliation note:
- Exports reflect Usage Insights attribution for the selected filters/time window.
- Invoices can differ due to billing period boundaries, credits/adjustments, minimum commits (Dedicated), taxes, and late-arriving usage.
Action: I’ll incorporate this into the export docs FAQ and share a snippet back to Finance for their internal one-pager.
resolution: Provided canonical definitions for cached token fields and guidance for Finance: cached token columns are supplemental diagnostics; any discounted compute attribution is already reflected in total_cost. Added reconciliation caveats (invoice vs console/exports) and examples suitable for internal chargeback guidance. PM to incorporate the same wording into public-facing export documentation/FAQ.
